chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Waddad Al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had sheep and had sheep, which he milked. A man would come to him and buy five hundred ratls and more than that, one hundred ratls, for such and such a price. He would take from him one hundred ratls every day until he had fulfilled what he had bought from him. He said, 'There is no harm with this.'

key_terms.رِطْلٍ: Ratl (a unit of weight used in Islamic jurisprudence for measuring goods)
key_terms.غَنَمٌ: Sheep (plural of shah, commonly used for small livestock including sheep and goats)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy milk by weight in advance and take it daily until the total amount is delivered?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the sale of milk by weight (ratl) where the buyer purchases a large aggregate quantity and receives it in fixed daily installments until the total is fulfilled. It illustrates the application of *al-gharar* (uncertainty) principles in Shia jurisprudence, confirming that such deferred delivery transactions are permissible provided the total quantity and price are known, thereby distinguishing them from invalid speculative sales.
